summary: P2 bounded pilot: Q ignorance versus strengthened negative truth, Q/R cancellation logic, and a finite pragmatic-labor interpreter. Relevance, norm observance, stereotype and corresponding alternatives are inputs, not derived from words.

sources.citation: Horn (1984), Toward a New Taxonomy for Pragmatic Inference, sections 1–11 pp.11–31; (12) pp.20–21 and (16)–(18) pp.22–23 visually checked.
sources.available: Local primary source read within the stated scope; source inventory and limitations recorded. Independent source review pending.

definitions_mapped.source: H1 p.13: added accessible-world encoding; competence is an EXTRA strengthening premise, not inferred from Q observance.
H2,H3 pp.20–21 (12): weaker content plus not-stronger versus stronger; conditional logical content, not automatic utterance interpretation.
H3 pp.14,20 (2a),(10): restricted natural-number lower bound with Q upper bound.
H4 pp.22–23 (17): added Boolean/default-context interpreter and finite enumeration; common extension, binary stereotypes and corresponding alternatives are supplied.

definitions_mapped.coq: Causatives.situation; literal; stereotype; normal; cancelled; no_counterpart
definitions_mapped.source: H5 pp.27–29: assigned two-state direct/indirect example, not general lexical semantics or synonym blocking.
H3 empirical restrictions on readings of negated utterances; H6 Q/R weighting, learned stereotypes, diachrony and general lexical selection.

theorems.name: q_yields_ignorance
theorems.source_claim: p.13 Q knowledge qualification: relevance, availability and norm observance plus non-use of a stronger form imply ignorance.

theorems.name: negative_truth_needs_strengthening
theorems.source_claim: Negative actual-world truth requires explicit competence and actual-world accessibility in addition to ignorance.

theorems.name: ignorance_compatible_with_strong_truth
theorems.source_claim: Two-world countermodel: ignorance of the stronger content can coexist with its actual truth.

theorems.name: descriptive_negation_excludes_stronger
theorems.source_claim: pp.20–21 (12): descriptive not-W entails not-S when S entails W.

theorems.name: stronger_forces_non_descriptive_rejection
theorems.source_claim: pp.20–21: affirmation of S excludes descriptive not-W; does not compute metalinguistic readings.

theorems.name: q_r_incompatible
theorems.source_claim: pp.20–21 (12): upper-bound and strengthened contents are logically incompatible.
theorems.note: H2 — direct source formalization; the vacuity probe intentionally flags the inconsistent Q/R premises. This is a disjointness result, not an inference from a consistent joint reading.

theorems.name: stronger_cancels_q_not_literal
theorems.source_claim: pp.20–21: stronger continuation rejects Q upper bound without rejecting literal W.

theorems.name: r_cancellation_preserves_literal
theorems.source_claim: p.21 (13): retaining W while cancelling R enrichment is logically possible.

theorems.name: reading_partition_requires_a_decision
theorems.source_claim: A logical partition requires a decision S or not-S; does not claim automatic pragmatic choice.

theorems.name: logical_entailment_does_not_ban_r_rejection
theorems.source_claim: Entailment-only countermodel, NOT a refutation of the empirical restriction on negated utterances.

theorems.name: Numerals.two_sided_is_exact
theorems.source_claim: Numeral lower bound plus next-value upper bound gives exact quantity.

theorems.name: Numerals.four_cancels_three_upper_bound
theorems.source_claim: p.20 (10a): four satisfies at-least-three while cancelling its upper bound.

theorems.name: Numerals.descriptive_not_three_excludes_four
theorems.source_claim: p.20 descriptive not-at-least-three excludes at-least-four.

theorems.name: Numerals.cancellation_is_not_descriptive_negation
theorems.source_claim: Upper-bound cancellation at four is not descriptive negation of at-least-three.

theorems.name: finite_readings_exact
theorems.source_claim: Finite enumeration exactly returns supplied-domain candidates satisfying the added acceptance predicate.

theorems.name: readings_preserve_literal
theorems.source_claim: The added interpreter preserves literal truth in its returned readings.

theorems.name: labor_disjoint_when_applicable
theorems.source_claim: pp.22–23 (17): disjoint stereotypical/non-stereotypical readings under explicitly supplied ordinary/counterpart conditions.

theorems.name: labor_covers_common_extension
theorems.source_claim: Binary supplied stereotype exhausts the chosen common extension; stronger than a general empirical exhaustivity claim.

theorems.name: context_cancellation_restores_literal
theorems.source_claim: Disabling ordinary defaults restores literal content in this interpreter.

theorems.name: no_counterpart_no_marked_exclusion
theorems.source_claim: Without a corresponding unmarked alternative the marked form is not automatically excluded from the stereotype.

theorems.name: Causatives.killed_caused_contrast
theorems.source_claim: p.27 (28): supplied direct/indirect kill/cause-to-die contrast.

theorems.name: Causatives.counterpart_and_context_matter
theorems.source_claim: Boundary tests withdrawing counterpart availability or ordinary context.

theorems.name: Causatives.same_extension_does_not_identify_readings
theorems.source_claim: Same supplied literal extension need not give identical pragmatic readings.

theorems.name: Causatives.removing_counterpart_restores_direct_case
theorems.source_claim: Removing the supplied corresponding alternative restores the direct case.

evidence: P2 bounded pilot: Q ignorance versus strengthened negative truth, Q/R cancellation logic, and a finite pragmatic-labor interpreter. Relevance, norm observance, stereotype and corresponding alternatives are inputs, not derived from words.
simplifications: H2,H3 pp.20–21 (12): weaker content plus not-stronger versus stronger; conditional logical content, not automatic utterance interpretation.
H3 pp.14,20 (2a),(10): restricted natural-number lower bound with Q upper bound.
omissions: H3: logical compatibility does not establish the empirical ban on R-cancelling negated readings.
H6: no Q/R weighting, empirical validation, learned stereotypes or diachrony; sections after 11 not read for this bounded campaign.
Causative contrast is illustrative; no automatic lexical correspondence or shorter-synonym blocking.
additions: H1 p.13: added accessible-world encoding; competence is an EXTRA strengthening premise, not inferred from Q observance.
H4 pp.22–23 (17): added Boolean/default-context interpreter and finite enumeration; common extension, binary stereotypes and corresponding alternatives are supplied.
H5 pp.27–29: assigned two-state direct/indirect example, not general lexical semantics or synonym blocking.

determination_rationale: Bounded attempt completed, not a completed source-theory formalization. Added machinery and uncovered core claims prevent a whole-source determination; these chosen restrictions do not show that restructuring was necessary.
